A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diffusion of atoms along grain boundaries in oxides and alkali halides is much faster than that along dislocations in these crystals and that the effective widths of grain boundaries are much larger than the radii of dislocations.
the short-circuit diffusion coefficients in the oxides and carbides are of the order of 10 ^{−4} cm ^{2} sec ^{−1}, and the effective diffusion width of the order of one lattice spacing.

the data for dislocation and grain boundaries are consistent with the idea that the short-circuit diffusion process is controlled by diffusion of point defects to the boundaries, and that the boundaries are not sinks or sources for point defects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion along grain boundaries and the diffusion along dislocations are not the same.
dislocation diffusion in oxides is much faster than grain boundary diffusion and the dislocation radius is much larger.
dislocation diffusion is a significant diffusion mechanism in many materials, and it is often the fastest diffusion mechanism, even when grain boundaries are present.
